correctness.rationale: PASS. Beatty complementarity partitions positive integers into lower and upper Wythoff sets; the upper-set indicator equals floor(delta(m+1))-floor(delta m). As floor(k phi²)<n iff 1<=k<=floor(delta n), the ordered count is exactly a bounded-rotation sum H_{y_n}({k phi}), where y_n={n delta}. The indicator H_y is a union of at most two intervals, and its interval integral is F(y)/delta: plateau F=delta for y<=1-2delta, descending branch F=1-delta-y for 1-2delta<=y<=1-delta, rising branch F=y-1+delta. The continued-fraction denominators of phi are Fibonacci numbers; every length-q block differs by O(1) from a translated grid with error uniformly in the starting phase. Zeckendorf decomposition into O(log n) such blocks gives discrepancy O(log n) uniformly in phase, not just asymptotic equidistribution. K_n=floor(delta n)=delta n+O(1) then proves r(n)-nF({n delta})=O(log n). The pushforward of circle-uniform phase by continuous F has plateau mass 1-2delta at delta and two branches mapping one-to-one to (0,delta) giving density 2. Combining pointwise normalized error sum O(log² X/X) with bounded-variation discrepancy O(log X/X) gives the claimed W1 bound. Independent direct convolution of both Beatty sequences for all n<=5000 gave maximum observed absolute profile error <1.869; the frozen verify.py uses different exact arithmetic and was directly read. Finite experiments do not prove the all-n discrepancy or convergence.
residual_risks: Uniform constant C not optimized and no bounded-error conjecture made. Irrational endpoints must be handled consistently in floor increments; the finite exact convolution and precise proof formula do so.
